state_machine.meaning: The signal is invalid; no hold is armed.
transitions: Valid signal without a valid-fault rising edge: go to READY.
Valid-fault rising edge: go to TRACKING and toggle timer selection.

state_machine.meaning: The signal is valid and no fault has triggered since the last invalid scan.
transitions: Valid-fault rising edge: go to TRACKING and toggle timer selection.

state_machine.meaning: A fault has triggered since the last invalid scan. The selected timer may be running or expired.
transitions: Valid-fault rising edge: remain TRACKING and toggle timer selection, restarting the hold.
Otherwise: remain TRACKING; timer expiry alone does not change state.

timers.name: HoldA
timers.IN: THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND state = TRACKING AND select_A
timers.reset: IN is FALSE, including on invalid signal or selection of HoldB.

timers.name: HoldB
timers.IN: THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND state = TRACKING AND NOT select_A
timers.reset: IN is FALSE, including on invalid signal or selection of HoldA.

timer_plan.operation: Toggle select_A on every valid-fault rising edge. The newly selected timer was disabled on the preceding scan, so its unconditional call starts at elapsed zero on the trigger scan. Alternation permits a fresh edge to restart the hold without calling a timer twice. Hold is active when TRACKING and the selected timer's Q is FALSE; it ends at 500 ms, unless invalidity cancels it sooner. Use elapsed timer time, not CycleTime, for the hold.

priorities: Signal invalidity immediately suppresses the alarm, cancels the hold, and prevents recording and runtime accumulation; existing statistics are preserved.
With a valid signal, a persistent fault keeps the alarm on regardless of timer expiry.
Every valid-fault rising edge records an occurrence and restarts the minimum hold.
Statistics and history are observational only and never affect cutting permissives. Expose history as read-only to callers.
UINT counter and LTIME runtime overflow are outside the bounded cases; establish a separate deployment policy.

internal.statistics_registers: Zero counter, runtime, and all five history elements.
internal.timers: Both TON instances initialized reset: Q = FALSE and ET = T#0ms.

initial_values.note: Initialization occurs before the first invocation; do not reinitialize statistics on the first scan or on signal loss.

scan_execution_order.name: Edge sampling
actions: Sample all inputs. Compute valid_fault = THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND THICKNESS_FAULT and rise = valid_fault AND NOT previous_valid_fault.
Set previous_valid_fault = valid_fault each scan, including invalid scans. Thus a fault present when validity returns is a new occurrence.

scan_execution_order.name: Safety/reset priority and state transitions
actions: Apply invalidity first: enter INHIBITED and cancel the logical hold. Otherwise apply the state transitions and toggle select_A on rise.
On rise, increment the internal counter once; shift history from index 3 to 4 down through index 0 to 1, then write the sampled FaultTimestamp to index 0.

When CUTTING_RUN AND THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND NOT THICKNESS_FAULT, add the current positive CycleTime to internal runtime after an exact widening to LTIME. Otherwise preserve runtime. This includes a qualifying first invocation.

scan_execution_order.name: Unconditional top-level timer FB calls
actions: Call HoldA and HoldB exactly once each scan, outside CASE and IF, using their specified IN expressions and PT values.
Read the selected timer's updated Q for this scan; timer expiry must affect the same observed scan.

scan_execution_order.name: Unified output assignments
actions: Assign THICKNESS_ALARM = THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND (THICKNESS_FAULT OR (state = TRACKING AND NOT selected_timer.Q)).
Assign the counter, runtime and history outputs from their internal registers in one output section.
